High up in the bright blue sky, all the young clouds were learning to make rain. They puffed up big and proud, letting gentle showers fall to the earth below. But little Nimbus tried and tried, and not a single drop came out.
1/10
The other clouds cheered as their rain made the gardens grow. Nimbus floated away to a quiet corner of the sky, feeling small and useless. 'Why can't I make rain like everyone else?' he whispered to the wind.
2/10
Just then, a big friendly cloud named Cumulus floated over. 'Hey there, little one,' he said warmly. 'I've seen you trying so hard. Maybe you're not broken — maybe you're just different in a wonderful way.'
3/10
Illustration unavailable
Cumulus guided Nimbus to look down at the world below. There, a beautiful meadow of flowers was drooping and thirsty. A tiny brown bird sat on a wilting sunflower, looking up at the sky with hopeful eyes.
4/10
Nimbus puffed himself up as big as he could. He scrunched his face and squeezed his eyes shut, trying so hard to make rain for the thirsty flowers. But still... not a single drop fell.
5/10
Then the tiny brown bird below began to sing the silliest, most wonderful song. It was so funny and sweet that Nimbus couldn't help it — a tiny giggle bubbled up inside him, then a chuckle, then a big, joyful belly laugh!
6/10
And then something magical happened! From Nimbus's happy tears of laughter, the most beautiful sparkling rain began to fall. Each drop shimmered with rainbow colors — pink, gold, blue, and green — twinkling like tiny jewels in the sunlight!
7/10
The rainbow rain touched the thirsty flowers, and they sprang back to life, more beautiful than ever! The little bird danced and sang, and the whole meadow sparkled with joy. Nimbus had never felt so happy!
8/10
Cumulus smiled proudly at his little friend. 'You see, Nimbus? You were never broken. Your rain comes from joy — and that makes it the most beautiful rain in the whole wide sky.' Nimbus beamed, glowing brighter than ever before.
9/10
From that day on, Nimbus traveled the sky bringing his sparkling rainbow rain to every thirsty garden and sad little flower. And he learned that being different isn't something to hide — it's the most wonderful gift of all. Because the best things in life come straight from a joyful heart!
10/10
